messages:
sam-support: Customer acct-492 reporting intermittent 403s from their app when traffic egresses via a central TGW NAT. Works from the public internet.

mike-customer: Seeing this response when the app calls our hosted API from the private subnet:
```
> POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
< HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
< content-type: application/json
< {\n  \"error\":\"invalid_origin\",\n  \"message\":\"token source IP mismatch\"\n}
```

mike-customer: Same bearer token from my laptop (public network) succeeds. Problem started after migrating egress to central TGW/NAT.

juan-sre: Two likely causes: token is bound to a caller IP (enterprise feature) and central NAT translates client IP to the NAT IP, or DNS/private routing is resolving our API to the VPCE but the traffic is being hairpinned through TGW/NAT instead of the direct ENI.

juan-sre: Quick repro steps to ask customer to run:
1) From a pod/instance in the affected subnet: `curl -v https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H \"Authorization: Bearer <token>\" -d '{\"prompt\":\"test\"}'` and also `curl -sS https://ifconfig.me` to show egress IP.
2) From a public host run the same curl and confirm it succeeds.
3) Paste the subnet route table and whether private DNS for `api.redwood.example` is enabled for the VPC.

chris-eng: Short-term mitigation suggestions: add the central NAT public IP to the account token/IP allowlist (e.g., 3.23.45.67) so requests are accepted while they evaluate a long-term change; or switch the token policy to remove IP binding.

chris-eng: Longer-term fixes: ensure calls to our API resolve to the VPCE and are routed directly to the interface endpoint in the same AZ (avoid TGW/NAT for that flow), or adopt an auth approach that doesn't rely on client IP (recommended for TGW/central egress setups). If they use PrivateLink, remember the source IP we see will be the VPCE ENI in our VPC — design allowlists accordingly.

juan-sre: Ask them to run tcpdump on the spoke instance to confirm path: `sudo tcpdump -nni eth0 host <VPCE_IP> and tcp port 443 -c 100 -w /tmp/redwood.pcap`. If packets show going to TGW/NAT instead of the ENI, that's the asymmetric/path issue.

mike-customer: Route table snippet: `0.0.0.0/0 -> tgw-rt-0a (propagated)`. Central NAT translates to 3.23.45.67. From a pod `curl https://ifconfig.me` returns `3.23.45.67`. We'll try adding that IP to allowlist as a temporary unblock and run tcpdump to confirm.

sam-support: I'll add the recommended temp workaround to the ticket and follow up for the pcap + final routing confirmation.

sre-bot: Ticket #SUP-492 updated: temp workaround suggested (add central NAT IP to allowlist). Please attach pcap and route tables for follow-up.

mike-customer: Thanks all — updating ticket once we validate.
